req.title: Health probe returns liveness
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /health/ with HTTP 200 and a status:'ok' JSON body.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET /health/ returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing status:'ok'. To achieve high mutation kill rate we need: (1) a positive EP test asserting exact status code 200 AND exact JSON body {'status':'ok'}; (2) a negative NEG test verifying that an unsupported method (POST) on /health/ returns 405, confirming the route is method-constrained; (3) a BVA test asserting the Content-Type header is application/json, catching mutations that change the response media type or body encoding; (4) a DT test asserting the response body keys and values exactly, catching mutations that change 'ok' to another string or add/remove keys; (5) a STC test verifying the endpoint is idempotent across two consecutive calls, catching stateful mutations. All tests use fastapi.testclient.TestClient with in-process import, exact-value assertions, and no placeholders.

tests.name: test_health_returns_200_and_status_ok
preconditions: FastAPI app is importable from main
health_route is registered on the app
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the imported app
trace: R-PLAYER-016: system shall respond to GET /health/ with HTTP 200 and status:'ok' JSON body
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_health_returns_200_and_status_ok():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/health/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body == {"status": "ok"}
    assert body["status"] == "ok"
    assert len(body) == 1

tests.name: test_health_body_exact_keys_and_value
preconditions: FastAPI app is importable from main
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the imported app
Parse JSON body and inspect keys and values individually
expected: JSON body has exactly one key: 'status'
Value of 'status' key is exactly the string 'ok' (not 'OK', not 'okay', not True)
trace: R-PLAYER-016: status:'ok' — exact string value and single-key body required
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_health_body_exact_keys_and_value():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/health/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    keys = list(body.keys())
    assert keys == ["status"]
    assert body["status"] == "ok"
    assert body["status"] != "OK"
    assert body["status"] != "okay"
    assert body["status"] != True
    assert isinstance(body["status"], str)

tests.name: test_health_idempotent_across_two_calls
preconditions: FastAPI app is importable from main
No state change expected between consecutive GET /health/ calls
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the imported app
expected: Both calls return identical JSON body {"status": "ok"}
trace: R-PLAYER-016: liveness probe must be deterministic and idempotent
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_health_idempotent_across_two_calls():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r1 = client.get("/health/")
    r2 = client.get("/health/")
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r1.json() == {"status": "ok"}
    assert r2.json() == {"status": "ok"}
    assert r1.json() == r2.json()

def test_health_wrong_path_returns_404():

    response = client.get("/health")
    assert response.status_code != 200
    assert response.status_code in (404, 307, 308)
